data.source_title: Stopping Hospital Infections With Environmental Services (SHINE): A Cluster-randomized Trial of Intensive Monitoring Methods for Terminal Room Cleaning on Rates of Multidrug-resistant Organisms in the Intensive Care Unit
data.locator: Methods, Study Design and Room Turnaround Time; Results, Room Turnaround Time (section heading in full text)
data.source_setting: Six ICUs at three US medical centers; median turnaround-time data available from two hospitals (A and B)
data.source_period: 12-month retrospective baseline followed by two sequential 6-month intervention periods separated by 2-month washout; published 2022
data.source_n: All terminal-cleaning events during the measured periods at hospitals A and B; event denominator not reported in inspected paper sections. Trial had 6 ICU clusters at 3 centers.
data.quantity: Terminal-cleaning elapsed time, defined by the paper as time from cleaning process start to cleaning process end
data.unit: minutes; medians and IQR by study period
data.source_evidence_basis: The paper explicitly defines its average room turnaround-time measure as elapsed time from start of the cleaning process to end of the cleaning process for all terminally cleaned rooms. At the two hospitals with baseline data, median TAT was 42.0 minutes (IQR 26.0–60.5) at baseline, 46.5 (27.0–76.0) during UV/F, and 43.0 (28.5–73.5) during ATP. This measure excludes departure-to-clean-start and clean-end-to-ready delay.
data.limitations: ICU terminal cleaning only; TAT denominator is not stated in the inspected report, and data came from two of three centers. Feedback and recleaning interventions may add cleaning time. It is a cleaning-process interval, not general inpatient vacancy-to-ready time.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Use as an external anchor for the terminal-cleaning-process interval only, with separate EVS response and post-clean release waits. Do not transfer to routine rooms or RWJ.
